Denmark became a member of the European Union in 1973 and signed the [Lisbon Treaty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lisbon_Treaty "Lisbon Treaty") in 2007.

Denmark was a founding member of the [European Free Trade Association](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Free_Trade_Association "European Free Trade Association") (EFTA). During the 1960s, the EFTA countries were often referred to as the [Outer Seven](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Outer_Seven "Outer Seven"), as opposed to the [Inner Six](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inner_Six "Inner Six") of what was then the [European Economic Community](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Economic_Community "European Economic Community") (EEC).[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Denmark#cite_note-68) In 1973, along with Britain and Ireland, Denmark joined the European Economic Community (now the [European Union](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Union "European Union")) after a [public referendum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1972_Danish_European_Communities_membership_referendum "1972 Danish European Communities membership referendum"). The [Maastricht Treaty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maastricht_Treaty "Maastricht Treaty"), which involved further European integration, [was rejected](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Danish_Maastricht_Treaty_referendum "1992 Danish Maastricht Treaty referendum") by the Danish people in 1992; it was only accepted after a [second referendum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1993_Danish_Maastricht_Treaty_referendum "1993 Danish Maastricht Treaty referendum") in 1993, which provided for [four opt-outs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Opt-outs_in_the_European_Union "Opt-outs in the European Union") from policies. The Danes rejected the euro as the national currency in [a referendum in 2000](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2000_Danish_euro_referendum "2000 Danish euro referendum"). Constitutional change in 1953 led to a [single-chamber](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unicameralism "Unicameralism") parliament elected by proportional representation, female accession to the Danish throne, and Greenland becoming an integral part of Denmark. The [centre-left](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Centre-left "Centre-left")[Social Democrats](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Social_Democrats_(Denmark) "Social Democrats (Denmark)") led a string of coalition governments for most of the second half of the 20th century, introducing the [Nordic welfare model](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nordic_model "Nordic model"). The [Liberal Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Venstre_(Denmark) "Venstre (Denmark)") and the [Conservative People's Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conservative_People's_Party_(Denmark) "Conservative People's Party (Denmark)") have also led [centre-right](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Centre-right "Centre-right") governments.[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Denmark#cite_note-69)[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Denmark#cite_note-70)[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Denmark#cite_note-71)

Located in [Northern Europe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Northern_Europe "Northern Europe"), on a latitude traversing southern [Alaska](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alaska "Alaska"), and being north of [Edmonton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edmonton "Edmonton"), Denmark[[N 6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Denmark#cite_note-proper-20) consists of the northern part of the [Jutland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jutland "Jutland") peninsula and an [archipelago](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Archipelago "Archipelago") of [406 islands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_islands_of_Denmark "List of islands of Denmark").[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Denmark#cite_note-islands-22) Of these, the largest island is [Zealand](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zealand "Zealand"), on which the capital [Copenhagen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Copenhagen "Copenhagen") is situated, on the same latitude as Moscow, and [Glasgow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glasgow "Glasgow"), followed by the [North Jutlandic Island](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/North_Jutlandic_Island "North Jutlandic Island"), [Funen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Funen "Funen"), and [Lolland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lolland "Lolland").[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Denmark#cite_note-75) The island of [Bornholm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bornholm "Bornholm"), and small [archipelago](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Archipelago "Archipelago") of [Ertholmene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ertholmene "Ertholmene") (_Christiansø_ colloqually, after its biggest islet), is located some 150 km east of the rest of the country, in the [Baltic Sea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baltic_Sea "Baltic Sea"). Many of the larger islands are connected by bridges; a [bridge-tunnel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/%C3%98resund_Bridge "Øresund Bridge") across the [Øresund](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/%C3%98resund "Øresund") connects Zealand with Sweden; the [Great Belt Fixed Link](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_Belt_Fixed_Link "Great Belt Fixed Link") connects Funen with Zealand; and the [Little Belt Bridge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Little_Belt_Bridge_(1970) "Little Belt Bridge (1970)") connects Jutland with Funen. [Ferries](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferry "Ferry") or [small aircraft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Small_aircraft "Small aircraft") connect to the smaller islands. The four [cities with populations over 100,000](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_cities_in_Denmark_by_population "List of cities in Denmark by population") are the capital Copenhagen on Zealand; [Aarhus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aarhus "Aarhus") and [Aalborg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aalborg "Aalborg") in Jutland; and [Odense](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Odense "Odense") on Funen.

[![Image 25: A labelled map of Denmark](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/f5/Da-map.png/250px-Da-map.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Da-map.png)

The metropolitan part occupies a total area of 42,943.9 [square kilometres](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Square_kilometre "Square kilometre") (16,581 sq mi).[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Denmark#cite_note-area-76) The area of inland water is 600 km 2 (232 sq mi).[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Denmark#cite_note-FOOTNOTEJensen199910-77) The size of the land area cannot be stated exactly since the ocean constantly erodes and adds material to the coastline, and because of human [land reclamation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Land_reclamation "Land reclamation") projects (to counter erosion). [Post-glacial rebound](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post-glacial_rebound "Post-glacial rebound") raises the land by a bit less than 1 cm (0.4 in) a year in the north and east, extending the coast. A circle enclosing the same area as Denmark would be 234 kilometres (145 miles) in [diameter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diameter "Diameter") with a [circumference](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Circumference "Circumference") of 736 km (457 mi) (land area only: 232.33 km (144.36 mi) and 730 km (454 mi) respectively). The land area is the size of the [Upper Peninsula of Michigan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Upper_Peninsula_of_Michigan "Upper Peninsula of Michigan"). It shares a border of 68 kilometres (42 mi) with Germany to the south and is otherwise surrounded by 8,750 km (5,437 mi) of tidal [shoreline](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shoreline "Shoreline") (including small [bays](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bay "Bay") and [inlets](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inlet "Inlet")).[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Denmark#cite_note-Nature_and_Environment-78) No location in Denmark is farther from the coast than 52 km (32 mi). On the south-west coast of Jutland, the tide is between 1 and 2 m (3.28 and 6.56 ft), and the tideline moves outward and inward on a 10 km (6.2 mi) stretch.[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Denmark#cite_note-79) Denmark's [territorial waters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Borders_of_Denmark "Borders of Denmark") total 105,000 square kilometres (40,541 square miles).

Denmark's northernmost point is [Skagen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Skagen "Skagen") point (the north beach of the Skaw) at 57° 45' 7" northern latitude; the southernmost is [Gedser](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gedser "Gedser") point (the southern tip of [Falster](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Falster "Falster")) at 54° 33' 35" northern latitude; the westernmost point is [Blåvandshuk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bl%C3%A5vandshuk "Blåvandshuk") at 8° 4' 22" eastern longitude; and the easternmost point is [Østerskær](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/%C3%98stersk%C3%A6r "Østerskær") at 15° 11' 55" eastern longitude. This is in the small [Ertholmene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ertholmene "Ertholmene") archipelago 18 kilometres (11 mi) north-east of Bornholm. The distance from east to west is 452 kilometres (281 mi), from north to south 368 kilometres (229 mi).[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Denmark#cite_note-80)

The highest natural point is [Møllehøj](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/M%C3%B8lleh%C3%B8j "Møllehøj"), at 170.86 metres (560.56 ft).[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Denmark#cite_note-81) Although this is by far the lowest high point in the Nordic countries and also less than half of the highest point in [Southern Sweden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/G%C3%B6taland "Götaland"), Denmark's general elevation in its interior is generally at a safe level from [rising sea levels](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sea_level_rise "Sea level rise"). [Lammefjorden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lammefjorden "Lammefjorden"), deeper than −7 m (−23 ft) (near Audebo), is the lowest point. A sizeable portion of Denmark's [terrain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Terrain "Terrain") consists of rolling [plains](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plain "Plain") whilst the coastline is sandy, with large [dunes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dune "Dune") in northern Jutland. Although once extensively forested, today Denmark largely consists of [arable land](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arable_land "Arable land"). - **Norway** – national instrument: the **Hardanger fiddle** (a bowed fiddle whose strings are traditionally gut, metal, or horsehair【7†L1-L4】).
